claim: Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) arises from collateral damage to peripheral afferent sensory neurons by anticancer pharmacotherapy, leading to debilitating neuropathic pain.
source: Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) arises from collateral damage to peripheral afferent sensory neurons by anticancer pharmacotherapy, leading to debilitating neuropathic pain.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about CIPN etiology.

claim: No effective treatment for CIPN exists, short of dose-reduction which worsens cancer prognosis.
source: No effective treatment for CIPN exists, short of dose-reduction which worsens cancer prognosis.
evidence: This is a statement of established clinical knowledge about CIPN treatment limitations.

claim: Daily treatment of rats with P7C3-A20 prevented behavioral and histologic indicators of peripheral neuropathy produced by paclitaxel.
source: Daily treatment of rats with the first-in-class NAMPT stimulator, P7C3-A20, prevented behavioral and histologic indicators of peripheral neuropathy
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript showing behavioral and histological outcomes.

claim: P7C3-A20 stimulated tissue NAD recovery in paclitaxel-treated rats.
source: Daily treatment of rats with the first-in-class NAMPT stimulator, P7C3-A20, prevented behavioral and histologic indicators of peripheral neuropathy, stimulated tissue NAD recovery
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data measuring NAD levels in tissues.

claim: P7C3-A20 improved general health of paclitaxel-treated rats.
source: Daily treatment of rats with the first-in-class NAMPT stimulator, P7C3-A20, prevented behavioral and histologic indicators of peripheral neuropathy, stimulated tissue NAD recovery, improved general health
evidence: This claim is supported by observational data on general health indicators presented in Table 1 and Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: P7C3-A20 abolished attrition produced by a near maximum-tolerated dose of paclitaxel.
source: Daily treatment of rats with the first-in-class NAMPT stimulator, P7C3-A20, prevented behavioral and histologic indicators of peripheral neuropathy, stimulated tissue NAD recovery, improved general health, and abolished attrition produced by a near maximum-tolerated dose of PTX.
evidence: This claim is supported by survival data presented in Figure 3F and 3G.

claim: Inhibition of NAMPT blocked P7C3-A20-mediated neuroprotection.
source: Inhibition of NAMPT blocked P7C3-A20-mediated neuroprotection
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data using FK866, a NAMPT inhibitor, presented in Figure 5.

claim: Supplementation with nicotinamide potentiated a subthreshold dose of P7C3-A20 to full efficacy.
source: whereas supplementation with the NAMPT substrate, nicotinamide, potentiated a subthreshold dose of P7C3-A20 to full efficacy.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 5D-F.

claim: P7C3-A20 blocked PTX-induced allodynia in tumored mice without reducing antitumoral efficacy.
source: Importantly, P7C3-A20 blocked PTX-induced allodynia in tumored mice without reducing antitumoral efficacy.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from xenograft studies presented in Figure 8D and 8E.

claim: Enhancement of NAMPT activity is a promising new therapeutic strategy to protect against anticancer drug-induced peripheral neurotoxicity.
source: These findings identify enhancement of NAMPT activity as a promising new therapeutic strategy to protect against anticancer drug-induced peripheral neurotoxicity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Paclitaxel is widely used for the treatment of breast, ovarian, lung, and pancreatic cancer.
source: The microtubule stabilizer, paclitaxel (PTX), is widely used for the treatment of breast, ovarian, lung, and pancreatic cancer (Rivera and Cianfrocca, 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Rivera and Cianfrocca, 2015.

claim: PTX often produces debilitating, dose-limiting peripheral neuropathy.
source: Despite its clinical effectiveness, however, PTX often produces debilitating, dose-limiting peripheral neuropathy.
evidence: This is established clinical knowledge about PTX side effects.

claim: CIPN is the most common nonhematologic side effect of anticancer pharmacotherapy that affects up to 90% of cancer patients.
source: Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN) is the most common nonhematologic side effect of anticancer pharmacotherapy that affects up to 90% of cancer patients (Grisold et al., 2012; Miltenburg and Boogerd, 2014; Windebank and Grisold, 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Grisold et al., 2012; Miltenburg and Boogerd, 2014; Windebank and Grisold, 2008.

claim: Damage to peripheral sensory neurons from anticancer treatment causes patients to experience stimulus-specific allodynia, tingling pain, numbness, and/or loss of sensory function, symmetrically-distributed largely in their hands and feet.
source: The damage to peripheral sensory neurons resulting from anticancer treatment causes patients to experience stimulus-specific allodynia (i.e. pain in response to innocuous stimuli), tingling pain, numbness, and/or loss of sensory function, that are symmetrically-distributed largely in their hands and feet (Speck et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Speck et al., 2013.

claim: The pain associated with CIPN intensifies with each cycle of chemotherapy and persists beyond the cancer treatment period, often indefinitely.
source: The pain associated with this neuropathy intensifies with each cycle of chemotherapy and persists beyond the cancer treatment period, often indefinitely, subjugating patients to a substandard quality of life both during and after treatment (Cavaletti and Marmiroli, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Cavaletti and Marmiroli, 2010.

claim: There are no effective treatments or preventions for CIPN.
source: As there are no effective treatments or preventions for CIPN, potentially life-saving cancer treatment must often be dose-reduced or discontinued, adversely affecting cancer prognosis and survival (Rivera and Cianfrocca, 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Rivera and Cianfrocca, 2015.

claim: Cancer treatment must often be dose-reduced or discontinued due to CIPN, adversely affecting cancer prognosis and survival.
source: As there are no effective treatments or preventions for CIPN, potentially life-saving cancer treatment must often be dose-reduced or discontinued, adversely affecting cancer prognosis and survival (Rivera and Cianfrocca, 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Rivera and Cianfrocca, 2015.

claim: P7C3 increased the number of newborn neurons in the mouse hippocampus.
source: Previously, an in vivo phenotypic screen searching for proneurogenic compounds revealed that the aminopropyl carbazole, P7C3, increased the number of newborn neurons in the mouse hippocampus (Pieper et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Pieper et al., 2010.

claim: P7C3 reduced apoptosis in differentiating neuronal progenitors, suggesting a neuroprotective effect that promoted survival of newborn neurons.
source: Subsequent experiments demonstrated that rather than increasing neurogenesis, P7C3 reduced apoptosis in differentiating neuronal progenitors, suggesting a neuroprotective effect that promoted survival of the newborn neurons.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from experimental observations cited from previous work.

claim: P7C3-A20 displayed strong neuroprotective efficacy in several models of neurodegeneration, including Parkinson's disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, traumatic brain injury, optic nerve injury, ischemic stroke, and sciatic nerve crush.
source: P7C3-A20, a structural analogue of P7C3, displayed strong neuroprotective efficacy in several models of neurodegeneration, including Parkinson's disease, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, traumatic brain injury, optic nerve injury, ischemic stroke, and sciatic nerve crush (De Jesús-Cortés et al., 2012; Kemp et al., 2015; Loris et al., 2017; Oku et al., 2017; Tesla et al., 2012; Wang et al., 2016a; Yin et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to De Jesús-Cortés et al., 2012; Kemp et al., 2015; Loris et al., 2017; Oku et al., 2017; Tesla et al., 2012; Wang et al., 2016a; Yin et al., 2014.

claim: P7C3-A20 is a first-in-class stimulator of nicotinamide phosphoribosyltransferase (NAMPT), the rate-limiting enzyme in the nicotinamide adenine nucleotide (NAD) salvage pathway.
source: Recent work identified P7C3-A20 as a first-in-class stimulator of nicotinamide phosphoribosyltransferase (NAMPT), the rate-limiting enzyme in the nicotinamide adenine nucleotide (NAD) salvage pathway (Wang et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Wang et al., 2014.

claim: P7C3-A20 protected peripheral sensory neurons from neurotoxicity induced by PTX and this protection required NAMPT activity.
source: Here, using an aggressive rodent model of CIPN, we report that P7C3-A20 protected peripheral sensory neurons from neurotoxicity induced by PTX and that this protection required NAMPT activity.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript, particularly Figure 5.

claim: P7C3-A20 did not interfere with the antitumor activity of PTX nor promote tumor growth.
source: Importantly, P7C3-A20 did not interfere with the antitumor activity of PTX nor promote tumor growth.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from xenograft studies presented in Figure 8.

claim: Adult male Sprague-Dawley rats received three injections of PTX (11.7 mg/kg/day, i.p.), administered every other day, for a total cumulative dose of 35 mg/kg.
source: Adult male Sprague-Dawley rats received three injections of PTX (11.7 mg/kg/day, i.p.), administered every other day, for a total cumulative dose of 35 mg/kg (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental protocol used in the study.

claim: Average body weights and circulating leukocytes maximally decreased by 16% and 60%, respectively, following PTX treatment.
source: As is typical with this dose of PTX (Cliffer et al., 1998), average body weights and circulating leukocytes maximally decreased by 16% and 60%, respectively, following which the animals began to recover (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B and C, and is consistent with a citation to Cliffer et al., 1998.

claim: Altered nociceptive thresholds to mechanical, thermal cold, and thermal heat stimulation are robust indicators of the development of peripheral neuropathy and commonly observed in patients with CIPN.
source: Altered nociceptive thresholds to mechanical, thermal cold, and thermal heat stimulation are robust indicators of the development of peripheral neuropathy and commonly observed in patients with CIPN (Argyriou et al., 2012; Dougherty et al., 2007; Dougherty et al., 2004; Kleggetveit et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Argyriou et al., 2012; Dougherty et al., 2007; Dougherty et al., 2004; Kleggetveit et al., 2012.

claim: PTX treatment of rats significantly reduced the thresholds for mechanical and cold stimuli to elicit a paw withdrawal response.
source: PTX treatment of rats significantly reduced the thresholds for mechanical and cold stimuli to elicit a paw withdrawal response. This increased sensitivity (allodynia) developed within 4 days and was sustained for over 3 weeks (Figure 1A–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A-F.

claim: PTX-treated rats developed a transient hypoalgesia (reduced sensitivity) to thermal heat stimulation.
source: By contrast, PTX-treated rats developed a transient hypoalgesia (reduced sensitivity) to thermal heat stimulation (Figure 1G–I).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1G-I.

claim: Differential sensitivities to external stimuli have been described in cancer patients receiving PTX as well as in rodent models that incorporate moderate to high cumulative PTX dosages.
source: Differential sensitivities to external stimuli have been described in cancer patients receiving PTX (Cata et al., 2006; Dougherty et al., 2004; Nahman-Averbuch et al., 2011) as well as in rodent models that incorporate moderate to high cumulative PTX dosages (Authier et al., 2000; Peters et al., 2007b).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Cata et al., 2006; Dougherty et al., 2004; Nahman-Averbuch et al., 2011; Authier et al., 2000; Peters et al., 2007b.

claim: Degeneration of intraepidermal nerve fibers (IENFs) is a signature of PTX-induced damage to peripheral nociceptive neurons.
source: Degeneration of intraepidermal nerve fibers (IENFs), the tortuous free nerve endings of nociceptive neurons that innervate the epidermal layer of peripheral tissues, is a signature of PTX-induced damage to peripheral nociceptive neurons (Jin et al., 2008; Krukowski et al., 2015; Liu et al., 2010; Siau et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Jin et al., 2008; Krukowski et al., 2015; Liu et al., 2010; Siau et al., 2006.

claim: PTX treatment significantly reduced IENF density by ~50% in biopsies from rat hindpaws and forepaws obtained on day 7.
source: PTX treatment significantly reduced IENF density by ~50% in biopsies from rat hindpaws and forepaws obtained on day 7, 3 days after the final PTX injection (Figure 1J and L).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1J and L.

claim: IENF degeneration was still evident more than 2 weeks after PTX treatment.
source: IENF degeneration was still evident more than 2 weeks later (Figure 1M), which also paralleled the persistent allodynia observed in the rats.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1M.

claim: ATF3 is up-regulated in peripheral and spinal neurons following neuronal injury or stress.
source: ATF3 is up-regulated in peripheral and spinal neurons following neuronal injury (e.g. axotomy) or stress (Tsujino et al., 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Tsujino et al., 2000.

claim: Moderate-to-high doses of PTX induce ATF3 expression in rat DRG neurons.
source: Moderate-to-high doses of PTX have been shown to induce ATF3 expression in rat DRG neurons (Liu et al., 2010; Peters et al., 2007a; Verheyen et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Liu et al., 2010; Peters et al., 2007a; Verheyen et al., 2012.

claim: PTX treatment produced a marked increase in the number of lumbar DRG neurons expressing ATF3 within 3 days after treatment.
source: PTX treatment produced a marked increase in the number of lumbar DRG neurons expressing ATF3 within 3 days after treatment (Figure 1K and N).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1K and N.

claim: P7C3-A20 treatment did not alter PTX-induced weight loss or leukopenia.
source: P7C3-A20 treatment did not alter PTX-induced weight loss or leukopenia (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B and C), suggesting no protection for rapidly dividing gastrointestinal epithelia or leukocytes.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B and C.

claim: P7C3-A20 prevented completely the development of PTX-induced mechanical allodynia and heat hypoalgesia, and markedly reduced cold allodynia.
source: Remarkably, however, P7C3-A20 prevented completely the development of PTX-induced mechanical allodynia and heat hypoalgesia, and markedly reduced cold allodynia (Figure 2A–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A-F.

claim: P7C3-A20 alone had no effect on nociceptive responses as compared to vehicle, indicating its action was not analgesic in nature.
source: P7C3-A20 alone had no effect on nociceptive responses as compared to vehicle, indicating its action was not analgesic in nature.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from experimental data comparing P7C3-A20 alone to vehicle.

claim: P7C3-A20 completely prevented PTX-induced IENF degeneration by day 7, and this protective effect was sustained through at least day 16.
source: In concordance with the results from the behavior experiments, P7C3-A20 completely prevented PTX-induced IENF degeneration by day 7, and this protective effect was sustained through at least day 16 (Figure 2G and I).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2G and I.

claim: P7C3-A20 partially reduced PTX-induced ATF3 expression from 33.4% to 20.6% of lumbar DRG neurons.
source: P7C3-A20 also partially reduced PTX-induced ATF3 expression from 33.4% to 20.6% of lumbar DRG neurons (Figure 2H and J).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2H and J.

claim: P7C3-A20 did not completely prevent the up-regulation of ATF3 by PTX treatment, suggesting that PTX still initiated a neuronal damage/stress response even in the presence of P7C3-A20.
source: It is noteworthy that P7C3-A20 did not completely prevent the up-regulation of ATF3 by PTX treatment, suggesting that, even in the presence of P7C3-A20, PTX still initiated a neuronal damage/stress response.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the ATF3 expression data.

claim: P7C3-A20 reduced PTX-induced mechanical and cold allodynia as well as IENF degeneration in a dose-dependent manner.
source: As before, P7C3-A20 reduced the PTX-induced mechanical and cold allodynia as well as IENF degeneration in a dose-dependent manner and consistent with plasma drug levels for each (Figure 3A–C and Figure 3—figure supplements 1 and 2, Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A-C and supplementary figures.

claim: P7C3-S321 was partially effective at preventing PTX-induced mechanical allodynia but did not reduce the cold allodynia.
source: P7C3-S321 was partially effective at preventing PTX-induced mechanical allodynia but did not reduce the cold allodynia.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data presented in Figure 3.

claim: Changes in nociceptive thresholds to mechanical and cold stimulation were strongly correlated with IENF density.
source: Changes in nociceptive thresholds to mechanical and cold stimulation were strongly correlated with IENF density (Figure 3D and E, Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 3D and E.

claim: Neither P7C3-A20 nor P7C3-S321 altered PTX-induced weight loss.
source: Despite the dramatic neuroprotective effect on PTX-induced allodynia and IENF density, neither P7C3-A20 nor P7C3-S321 altered PTX-induced weight loss, although the highest dose of P7C3-A20 (20 mg/kg/day) partially reduced leukopenia (Figure 3—figure supplement 3, Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: The highest dose of P7C3-A20 (20 mg/kg/day) partially reduced PTX-induced leukopenia.
source: Despite the dramatic neuroprotective effect on PTX-induced allodynia and IENF density, neither P7C3-A20 nor P7C3-S321 altered PTX-induced weight loss, although the highest dose of P7C3-A20 (20 mg/kg/day) partially reduced leukopenia (Figure 3—figure supplement 3, Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: P7C3-A20 improved indices of general animal health more so than P7C3-S321.
source: Observationally, P7C3-A20, more so than P7C3-S321, improved indices of general animal health (Table 1 and Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This claim is supported by observational data presented in Table 1 and Figure 3—figure supplement 4.

claim: P7C3-A20 substantially reduced attrition rates across all behavioral experiments.
source: Furthermore, P7C3-A20 substantially reduced attrition rates across all behavioral experiments (Figure 3F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Study attrition was 25% for rats treated with PTX alone, where death almost always occurred within days 8 and 11 of the experimental paradigm.
source: Study attrition was 25% for rats treated with PTX alone, where death almost always occurred within days 8 and 11 of the experimental paradigm (Figure 3G).
evidence: This claim is supported by survival data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: No deaths occurred in rats treated with P7C3-A20 at doses of at least 6.6 mg/kg/day.
source: In stark contrast, no deaths occurred in rats treated with P7C3-A20 at doses of at least 6.6 mg/kg/day.
evidence: This claim is supported by survival data presented in the manuscript.

claim: FK866 completely blocked the protective effects of P7C3-A20 on PTX-induced mechanical allodynia and IENF degeneration.
source: However, FK886 completely blocked the protective effects of P7C3-A20 on PTX-induced mechanical allodynia and IENF degeneration (Figure 5B and C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C), suggesting that NAMPT activity is required for the neuroprotective effect of P7C3-A20 on PTX-induced peripheral neuropathy.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B, C and supplementary figures.

claim: NAMPT activity is required for the neuroprotective effect of P7C3-A20 on PTX-induced peripheral neuropathy.
source: However, FK886 completely blocked the protective effects of P7C3-A20 on PTX-induced mechanical allodynia and IENF degeneration (Figure 5B and C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1C), suggesting that NAMPT activity is required for the neuroprotective effect of P7C3-A20 on PTX-induced peripheral neuropathy.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the FK866 inhibition experiments.

claim: NAM supplementation enhanced the neuroprotective efficacy of subthreshold P7C3-A20 (2.2 mg/kg/day) to a degree equivalent to that produced by the highest dose of P7C3-A20 (20 mg/kg/day).
source: However, NAM supplementation enhanced the neuroprotective efficacy of subthreshold P7C3-A20 (2.2 mg/kg/day) in both behavioral and anatomical indices of neuropathy to a degree equivalent to that produced by the highest dose of P7C3-A20 (20 mg/kg/day) (Figure 5E and F and Figure 5—figure supplement 2B and C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5E, F and supplementary figures.

claim: NAMPT activity is critical for the neuroprotective efficacy of P7C3-A20 against PTX-induced neuronal damage and peripheral neuropathic pain.
source: These results taken together reveal a critical contribution of NAMPT activity to the neuroprotective efficacy of P7C3-A20 against PTX-induced neuronal damage and peripheral neuropathic pain.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the FK866 and NAM supplementation experiments.

claim: P7C3-A20 dose-dependently increased H2O2-depleted NAD levels back to vehicle-treated baseline in A1A1 rat cortical neurons.
source: While P7C3-A20 or NAM did not increase NAD production in vehicle-treated cells (Figure 6A), P7C3-A20 dose-dependently increased H2O2-depleted NAD levels back to vehicle-treated baseline (Figure 6B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The rescue of NAD levels in H2O2-treated cells by P7C3-A20 was blocked by FK866.
source: The rescue of NAD levels in H2O2-treated cells was blocked by FK866 (Figure 6C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: P7C3-A20 stimulates NAD recovery through NAMPT in neuronal cells, but this effect occurred only in cells depleted of NAD.
source: These data suggest that P7C3-A20 stimulates NAD recovery through NAMPT in neuronal cells, but this effect occurred only in cells depleted of NAD.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the in vitro NAD measurement experiments.

claim: PTX treatment alone reduced NAD+ levels in the hindpaw and sciatic nerve, which was abolished by P7C3-A20 treatment.
source: PTX treatment alone reduced NAD+ levels in the hindpaw and sciatic nerve, which was abolished by P7C3-A20 treatment (Figure 7A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A and B.

claim: NAD+ levels in the DRG were unaffected by either PTX or P7C3-A20.
source: NAD+ levels in the DRG were unaffected by either drug (Figure 7C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7C.

claim: P7C3-A20 augments NAMPT-mediated NAD production in peripheral sensory neurons in response to the damaging effects of PTX.
source: Collectively, these data further support the hypothesis that P7C3-A20 augments NAMPT-mediated NAD production in peripheral sensory neurons in response to the damaging effects of PTX.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the tissue NAD measurement experiments.

claim: P7C3-A20 did not change the anti-proliferative or cytotoxic potency or efficacy of PTX in cancer cell lines.
source: P7C3-A20 did not change the anti-proliferative or cytotoxic potency or efficacy of PTX, nor did it alter the microtubule-stabilizing properties of PTX (Figure 8A and B and Figure 8—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8A, B and supplementary figures.

claim: P7C3-A20 did not alter the microtubule-stabilizing properties of PTX.
source: P7C3-A20 did not change the anti-proliferative or cytotoxic potency or efficacy of PTX, nor did it alter the microtubule-stabilizing properties of PTX (Figure 8A and B and Figure 8—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8A, B and supplementary figures.

claim: PTX treatment markedly decreased tumor growth in MDA-MB-231 xenografts.
source: PTX treatment markedly decreased tumor growth as expected. P7C3-A20 did not alter the antitumor effects of PTX, nor alter tumor growth when administered alone (Figure 8D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8D.

claim: P7C3-A20 did not alter the antitumor effects of PTX in MDA-MB-231 xenografts.
source: PTX treatment markedly decreased tumor growth as expected. P7C3-A20 did not alter the antitumor effects of PTX, nor alter tumor growth when administered alone (Figure 8D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8D.

claim: P7C3-A20 did not alter tumor growth when administered alone in MDA-MB-231 xenografts.
source: PTX treatment markedly decreased tumor growth as expected. P7C3-A20 did not alter the antitumor effects of PTX, nor alter tumor growth when administered alone (Figure 8D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8D.

claim: P7C3-A20 completely prevented PTX-induced mechanical allodynia in tumor-bearing mice.
source: As with its effect in rats, P7C3-A20 completely prevented PTX-induced mechanical allodynia in the tumor-bearing mice (Figure 8E and Figure 8—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 8E and supplementary figures.

claim: P7C3-A20 treatment can attenuate the deleterious effects of PTX on peripheral nociceptive neurons and mitigate peripheral neuropathic pain without compromising the desired antitumor effects.
source: Collectively, these results demonstrate that P7C3-A20 treatment can attenuate the deleterious effects of PTX on peripheral nociceptive neurons and mitigate peripheral neuropathic pain without compromising the desired antitumor effects.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the xenograft and cancer cell line experiments.

claim: High-dose PTX treatment produced transient but substantial average weight loss of 16% and average leukocyte depletion of 60%.
source: High-dose PTX treatment (cumulative dose of 35 mg/kg, i.p.) produced transient but substantial average weight loss of 16% and average leukocyte depletion of 60%.
evidence: This is a summary of experimental data presented earlier in the manuscript.

claim: Indices of general health were poor and attrition due to PTX toxicity was 25%.
source: Indices of general health were poor and attrition due to PTX toxicity (death or weight loss >20%) was 25%.
evidence: This is a summary of experimental data presented earlier in the manuscript.

claim: PTX treatment produced marked peripheral neuropathy evidenced by prolonged changes in the sensitivity to mechanical, cold and heat stimuli, by prolonged degeneration of IENFs, and by increased expression of ATF3 in the DRG.
source: As is typical of CIPN (Cata et al., 2006; Dougherty et al., 2004; Nahman-Averbuch et al., 2011), PTX treatment also produced marked peripheral neuropathy evidenced by prolonged changes in the sensitivity to mechanical, cold and heat stimuli, by prolonged degeneration of IENFs, and by increased expression of the neuronal injury marker, ATF3, in the DRG.
evidence: This is a summary of experimental data presented earlier in the manuscript, with citations to support the typicality of these findings.

claim: Daily treatment with P7C3-A20 (≥10 mg/kg/day, i.p.), beginning a few days before PTX administration, greatly reduced or eliminated the behavioral and anatomical signs of peripheral neuropathy.
source: Daily treatment with P7C3-A20 (≥10 mg/kg/day, i.p.), beginning a few days before PTX administration, greatly reduced or eliminated the behavioral and anatomical signs of peripheral neuropathy.
evidence: This is a summary of experimental data presented earlier in the manuscript.

claim: The neuroprotective effects of P7C3-A20 were replicated consistently over several independent, blinded behavioral experiments and across two different species.
source: The neuroprotective effects were replicated consistently over several independent, blinded behavioral experiments and across two different species.
evidence: This is a summary statement about the reproducibility of the experimental findings.

claim: P7C3-A20 demonstrated superior efficacy compared with PARP inhibitor A-861696 in the aggressive CIPN model.
source: P7C3-A20 also demonstrated superior efficacy in our aggressive model as compared with PARP inhibitor, A-861696, which previously was shown to protect against cisplatin-, oxaliplatin-, and vincristine-induced peripheral neuropathy (Brederson et al., 2012; Ta et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing P7C3-A20 and A-861696, with citations to previous work on A-861696.

claim: A-861696 previously was shown to protect against cisplatin-, oxaliplatin-, and vincristine-induced peripheral neuropathy.
source: P7C3-A20 also demonstrated superior efficacy in our aggressive model as compared with PARP inhibitor, A-861696, which previously was shown to protect against cisplatin-, oxaliplatin-, and vincristine-induced peripheral neuropathy (Brederson et al., 2012; Ta et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Brederson et al., 2012; Ta et al., 2013.

claim: P7C3-A20 improved the overall health of PTX-treated rats and reduced attrition to zero.
source: P7C3-A20 also improved the overall health of the PTX-treated rats and reduced attrition to zero.
evidence: This is a summary of experimental data presented earlier in the manuscript.

claim: P7C3-A20 treatment did not reduce the antiproliferative or cytotoxic efficacy of PTX in cell culture models.
source: Importantly, P7C3-A20 treatment did not reduce the antiproliferative or cytotoxic efficacy of PTX in cell culture models nor its antitumoral activity in an aggressive xenograft model in vivo.
evidence: This is a summary of experimental data presented earlier in the manuscript.

claim: P7C3-A20 treatment did not reduce the antitumoral activity of PTX in an aggressive xenograft model in vivo.
source: Importantly, P7C3-A20 treatment did not reduce the antiproliferative or cytotoxic efficacy of PTX in cell culture models nor its antitumoral activity in an aggressive xenograft model in vivo.
evidence: This is a summary of experimental data presented earlier in the manuscript.

claim: NAMPT is the rate-limiting enzyme in the salvage pathway for NAD production.
source: P7C3-A20 is a first-in-class stimulator of NAMPT (Wang et al., 2014), the rate-limiting enzyme in the salvage pathway for NAD production (Belenky et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Wang et al., 2014 and Belenky et al., 2007.

claim: There is increasing evidence that stimulation or maintenance of NAD biosynthesis is neuroprotective in a variety of experimental models of neurodegeneration.
source: There is increasing evidence that stimulation or maintenance of NAD biosynthesis is neuroprotective in a variety of experimental models of neurodegeneration (Cantó et al., 2015; Verdin, 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Cantó et al., 2015; Verdin, 2015.

claim: WldS mice exhibit marked protection from injury-induced axonal degeneration due to increased cytosolic levels of chimeric nicotinamide mononucleotide adenylyltransferase1.
